project.name: content-api
project.description:
Service-to-service contract for the content domain (V9 §18 / §91).
Members: BlogPublisher (the publish SPI), PublishCommand, PublishResult, PublishingLimits. These were reached for from a different future deployment unit: the CSDN and Juejin adapters live in the integration domain (dinqor-platform-integration) and implemented an interface owned by publishing (dinqor-content-automation). After the split that is a dependency pointing the wrong way across a service boundary, so the port and its data move to a module both sides may depend on.
Members added in the media cut: MediaAssetPort, MediaAssetRef, StoredImage. Callers live in three deployment units (agent / blogagent / studio) and previously imported the concrete @Service BlogMediaService plus the MyBatis entity BlogMediaAsset. The entity cannot be a contract type at all -- it carries @TableName / @TableId -- so it stays in publishing.domain and the service maps it at the boundary.
This cut also broke a cycle. BlogMediaService took blogagent.infrastructure.BlogAgentImageClient.GeneratedImage, so the content domain imported blogagent while blogagent imported BlogMediaService. The port now takes byte[] + contentType instead: the content domain only ever used those two fields, and the rest of GeneratedImage (usage / model / extension) stays with the producer. GeneratedImage itself could not move here -- it carries com.xander.lab.common.ModelUsage, which is Jackson-bearing.
Members added in the post cut: ContentPostPort, PublicationPort, ContentPost, ContentPostPage, ContentPostInput, ContentPostQuery, ContentPostStatus. Before it, three deployment units imported publishing.application.BlogService directly (integration 5 impl + 11 api, agent 3 + 3, profile 1). BlogService cannot move here: it is a @Service holding four MyBatis mappers, UserLookupPort and StringRedisTemplate. So it keeps its old public signatures as thin ThreadLocal-reading shells -- the 17 same-domain call sites in BlogController are untouched -- and implements the port. Every port method takes userId explicitly, because a ThreadLocal cannot cross a process.
ContentPost / ContentPostPage are mirrors, not narrowings: same names, same types, same order as BlogPostVO / PageData, minus tagsRaw. That makes the cut provably a pure refactor (the wire JSON is byte-identical), which is what keeps it out of docs/contract-changes.yaml. The mirror is proven by ContentPostShapeTest in apps/core-host (the contract cannot see BlogPostVO), including the production mapping itself.
Three DTOs exist here solely to kill adjacent same-typed positional parameters, which the compiler cannot protect: ContentPostInput replaced five adjacent Strings (summary/content swap silently puts the article body in the summary column), ContentPostQuery replaced two adjacent Booleans (juejin/csdn swap is silent, both SQLs return non-empty results), and ContentPostStatus replaced a string-to-int vocabulary that two agent tools had each written out. Component order in all of them is a positional contract; every one is pinned by reflection plus "the adjacent literals must differ".
PublicationPort was shaped to be isomorphic to PublicationService, so the implementation needed implements + @Override and zero body edits. Choosing a port shape is a design freedom -- prefer the one that makes the implementation change degenerate into a type substitution.
Two architectural decisions are frozen here and enforced by this module's package-info: ADR-1, contracts stay serialization-framework agnostic (no Jackson, no annotations on DTOs, no JsonNode); ADR-2, cross-domain traffic uses consumer-owned contracts and domain entities never cross a bounded-context boundary. A third one is still open: whether a contract may depend on another contract. Today the gate says no, which is why StoredImage exists rather than reusing integration.api.UploadResponse.
Zero dependencies, and that is the point. A contract that drags in a framework cannot be depended on by every service, and V9 §19 is explicit that the WebFlux Gateway must stay free of spring-webmvc. Nothing here may gain a compile dependency without a deliberate decision; test scope is fine.
What is deliberately NOT here yet: - publishing.api.BlogPostDTO / BlogPostVO. They already live in the domain's api layer, which the cross-domain scanner classifies as contract surface rather than as backlog, so moving them would change no measured number. They are also the *frontend* HTTP contract (web / miniprogram), a different audience from the service-to-service one. They join this module when the domain's api layer itself is split, in Wave 2. Note BlogPostVO is simultaneously the MyBatis projection target of BlogPostMapper (@JsonIgnore tagsRaw = GROUP_CONCAT result), so that split has to separate the wire shape from the persistence projection first.
Known residual after the post cut (recorded, not fixed): PublishPostTool still imports publishing.api.BlogPostVO, because BlogAgentService.publish / findPublishedPost return it. That keeps one api statement on the agent -> publishing edge with zero implementation statements. Closing it means changing BlogAgentService's public return type and BlogAgentController's -- a blogagent-vs-publishing decision, not a BlogService one. See docs/migration/adr-contract-boundaries.md section 5.10.
What is NOT a defect but is a real decision point: BlogPublisher is collected by Spring as a plain List and its implementations live in another future deployment unit. That works in one process and cannot work across two. Recorded in docs/migration/lib-extraction.md; it must be decided before Wave 2.
